Test a simple baseline mean combination to confirm weighted advantage and gauge performance on a non‑seasonal trend‑strong series.
The series shows moderate ranking stability and several correlated error groups; a DBA that can adapt to group structure may improve over simple weighted.
Explore a per‑horizon weighting to capture the fact that different models dominate at different horizons in this strong seasonal, trend‑heavy series.
The series has high trend and seasonality but ranking stability is moderate; a robust non‑weighted scheme like median on a small, correlated‑error pool might reduce variance.
try a weighted softmax_neg_error over the full pool to see if a smooth weighting beats median pool4.
The series shows strong trend and seasonality but moderate ranking stability; try a trimmed mean to reduce influence of outlier models.
Try a weighted combination on the smaller, high‑performing pool4 using inverse_error weights to see if a tighter pool with error‑based weighting improves over median pool4.
Try a DBA combination on the stable pool4 to see if a constrained aggregation improves over weighted approaches, given the moderate ranking stability and strong trend/seasonality.
Test a simple median over the full pool to see if the robust central tendency beats the weighted pool4 winner, given the strong trend and moderate ranking stability.
try a per-horizon weighted combo on the stable pool4 to capture horizon‐specific strengths, given moderate ranking stability and strong seasonality.
Test a simple mean combination on the reduced pool4 to see if averaging the best correlated models improves over weighted (different strategy type).

decision.justification: Selected 'median on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.1924. Series context: trend strength 0.9974 and seasonal strength 0.7886; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.462); 6 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 26.984.
